test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-II Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2025)
subject: general
question: Under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) registration may be cancelled if _______.

options.text: The Overseas Citizen of India formally seeks dual citizenship status
The Overseas Citizen of India permanently relocates to another country
The Overseas Citizen of India violates the Citizenship Act or any notified law
The Overseas Citizen of India refuses to comply with tax obligations

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Overseas Citizen of India violates the Citizenship Act or any notified law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019** stipulates that the registration of an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) can be cancelled if the individual violates **any provisions of the Citizenship Act, 1955** or any other **notified law**.
 
• Section 7D of the **Citizenship Act, 1955** provides the legal grounds for cancellation of OCI registration, including cases where the person has acted against the sovereignty, integrity, security, or interests of India.
 
• The cancellation of OCI registration is typically reserved for **serious violations** of laws, which may include acts that jeopardize national security, public order, or the rule of law in India.
 
• Such cancellation is conducted through a due process and is subject to an **opportunity for the individual to present their case** before the authorities.
 
• It is essential for OCI holders to comply with Indian laws and regulations, as the OCI status does not grant immunity from legal consequences in case of violations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Scheme:**

 
 
• OCI is a **long-term visa** scheme introduced by the Government of India under the Citizenship Act, 1955.
 
• It allows persons of Indian origin residing abroad to enjoy certain rights in India, such as visa-free travel and exemption from registration with police authorities for stays longer than 180 days.
 
• OCI cardholders can engage in activities such as buying property and pursuing education in India but are restricted from voting, holding public office, and working in government jobs.
 
 
 
• **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019:**
 
 
• The act amended the **Citizenship Act, 1955** to provide Indian citizenship to persecuted minorities (Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians) from **Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Bangladesh** who entered India before December 31, 2014.
 
• It excludes certain categories such as **Muslims** and has been a subject of political and social debates.
 
 
 
• **Key Restrictions for OCI Cardholders:**
 
 
• OCI holders are prohibited from **voting in Indian elections**, holding constitutional posts, or acquiring agricultural properties.
 
• They cannot participate in political activities or work in government sectors.
 
• Any violation of Indian laws, especially those affecting sovereignty or security, could lead to the cancellation of OCI registration.
 
 
 
• **Section 7D of Citizenship Act, 1955:**
 
 
• It defines the circumstances under which the registration of an OCI can be cancelled, including:
 
 
• If the registration was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation.
 
• If the individual violates **any provisions of the Citizenship Act** or other laws notified by the central government.
 
• If the individual has shown disloyalty or hostility towards India.
 
 
 
• Cancellation under Section 7D is subject to **legal procedures**, ensuring that the individual has a chance to defend themselves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cancellation Process:**

 
 
• OCI registration can only be cancelled after following a due process, including providing the individual with an opportunity to explain their actions.
 
• The decision is taken by the **central government**, and the reasons for cancellation must be clearly documented.
 
 
 
• **Safeguards for OCI Holders:**
 
 
• The cancellation of OCI registration is a serious action and is not undertaken for minor infractions or violations.
 
• It is reserved for cases involving fraud, severe legal violations, or actions against national interests.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework:**
 
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, along with its amendments, provides the legal basis for managing citizenship and OCI registrations.
 
• Section 7D of the act is pivotal in defining the grounds and procedures for cancellation.
